gre.detail: Official page: test scores are not required but applicants may submit GMAT or GRE to enhance the application. UF code 5812.

gmat.detail: Same as GRE: not required; optional submission of GMAT or GRE allowed (UF code 5812).

toefl.detail: UF Admissions international graduate page lists TOEFL iBT & Home Edition minimum 4.5 overall; subsections Reading/Listening/Speaking/Writing each 4.0 (new TOEFL scale as posted). School code 5812. Required for international applicants unless exemption applies.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5 via IELTS Results Service E-Delivery to University of Florida.

english.waiver: UF may exempt applicants from countries where English is the only official language; those who attended non-U.S. institutions where English is the only official language of instruction; or who earned a degree in the U.S. / English-only-official-language country / English-only-instruction institution (see UF Grad International exemptions list). Warrington FinTech page also refers applicants to UF international English requirements.

gpa.detail: 3.0 upper-division undergraduate GPA required (U.S. degrees only, per FinTech application requirements).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Two recommenders who have supervised the applicant (professor, employer, adviser, volunteer coordinator). Letters from students, peer leaders, or relatives not accepted. Contacts entered in application; recommenders emailed after submission.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Statement of purpose 400–600 words: motivations, candidacy, how program advances career goals.

resume.detail: 1–2 page resume/CV covering post-high school education and employment, international affiliations/research funding, experience, accomplishments, leadership, and outside commitments (Florida Statute / UF graduate requirement also applies).

transcripts.detail: Upload transcripts (English and native language) from all post-secondary institutions. Unofficial OK for review; official required in first term if admitted. UF students: do not submit UF transcript.

interview.detail: Warrington interviews candidates who attended a non-U.S. institution as part of admissions.

applicationFee.waivers: UF Office of Admissions does not provide graduate application fee waivers.
applicationFee.detail: $30 non-refundable Graduate School application fee per program (UF Admissions how-to-apply).

other: Bachelor’s from accredited institution; business major preferred (other majors case-by-case).
Graduate School application + Information for Residency Classification.
International: UF does not recognize 3-year bachelor’s from India, Australia, Bangladesh, Canada (excl. Quebec), Nepal, Pakistan; other 3-year degrees reviewed individually.
International: upload diploma/degree certification (English + native); letter of expected graduation if diploma not yet received.

gre.detail: No MS-QFIN-specific GRE policy found on official catalog or Artsci Math QFIN page as of scrape. Do not reuse classic tamu-msf 4+1 GRE rules. Confirm via Adam C. Sinn Department of Finance / BusinessCAS.

gmat.detail: Not stated on MS-QFIN catalog or Artsci QFIN page.

ielts.detail: Not stated on MS-QFIN-specific official pages reviewed.

english.waiver: Unknown for MS-QFIN; not invented from other Mays programs.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Not listed on MS-QFIN catalog / Artsci pages.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Not listed on MS-QFIN catalog / Artsci pages.

resume.detail: Not listed on MS-QFIN catalog / Artsci pages.

transcripts.detail: Not itemized on MS-QFIN catalog page; expect standard graduate transcript upload via application system—confirm BusinessCAS checklist.

interview.detail: Not stated on MS-QFIN official pages reviewed.

applicationFee.detail: Fee not posted on MS-QFIN catalog/Artsci pages; Mays master’s applications processed via BusinessCAS (mays.tamu.edu/apply)—confirm current BusinessCAS fee at submission.

other: Catalog eligibility OPEN to current TAMU sophomores/juniors/seniors OR non-Texas A&M graduates with equivalent prerequisites (ACCT 209 or 229/640; ECON 202 or 203; MATH 171+172 or 151+152 or equivalents) with B or higher by end of TAMU spring immediately following admission.
Highly recommended: Linear Algebra, Differential Equations, Statistics, coding experience.
36-hour non-thesis joint Finance + Mathematics (“STEM to Stocks”).

applicationRequirements.advice: OPEN external/intl per catalog. Fall 2027 application dates/requirements checklist not posted on dedicated QFIN marketing page as of 2026-10-27—flag gap; contact Finance (Jose Quiros) / BusinessCAS before applicant-facing claims. Never conflate with restricted tamu-msf.

gre.detail: Require GMAT, GMAT Focus, GRE, or GRE General Test at home (valid 5 years; for Spring 2027 entry not older than Jan 1, 2022). Optional only if (a) PhD earned/will earn before MFE start, OR (b) U.S. four-year bachelor with final cumulative GPA ≥3.70/4.00 (no rounding; non-U.S. bachelor and non-4.0 scales ineligible). Committee may still request a score. GRE codes 4833 / dept 4399.

gmat.detail: GMAT or GMAT Focus accepted interchangeably with GRE under same required/optional-eligibility rules above. Send to UC Berkeley Haas MFE.

toefl.detail: TOEFL iBT/Home Edition minimum 90 (institution 4833, dept 82). MyBest and TOEFL ITP/Duolingo not accepted. Haas Knowledge also notes revised TOEFL scale ≥4.5 for exams after January 2026—confirm which scale applies to Spring 2028 entry when registering.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic overall BAND ≥7; TOEFL preferred. Send TRF electronically to UC Berkeley Graduate Division.

english.waiver: Degree from country where official language is English; OR ≥1 year full-time coursework with grades B or better at a U.S. university (ESL/non-English/nonacademic/future courses excluded). Degrees from listed regions (e.g. India, PRC, Taiwan, most of Europe, etc.) do not meet country waiver even if instruction was English.

gpa.detail: Satisfactory scholastic average, usually minimum 3.0 in upper-division work (Haas MFE requirements).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Two letters from academic or professional evaluators of quantitative ability. Co-workers/tutors/friends/family inadmissible. Professional email required (no free personal providers per Haas Knowledge).

statementOfPurpose.detail: Series of essay questions in application; anti-plagiarism screening. Supplemental Information questions required (N/A if not applicable). Reapplicants within 2 years have special instructions.

resume.detail: Resume/CV not separately named on the requirements overview; work experience preferred but not required—confirm checklist in online application.

transcripts.detail: Scans of official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate programs attended. Degree from accredited institution before MFE start.

interview.detail: Invitation-only; do not request. May cover prerequisites/resume topics; sometimes more than one interview. Interviewers are not the admissions committee.

applicationFee.waivers: Not detailed on MFE requirements page beyond ETS GRE fee reduction partnership context.
applicationFee.detail: Non-refundable $275 application fee (credit card preferred; check/money order to UC Regents).

other: Video essay required (webcam/mic; up to 2 attempts; ≤2 minutes).

Prerequisites: strong quant background (linear algebra, multivariate calculus, differential equations, numerical analysis, advanced stats/probability); programming exposure (C++, Python); stats/econometrics (e.g. R); ML concepts.
SPRING-ONLY start (January); no Fall admission. Full-time 1-year and Flex 2-year both spring start.
Spring 2028 rounds: Dec 1 2026; Jan 27; Apr 1; Jul 1 2027 (late to Jul 15 space-available).
applicationRequirements.advice: Spring-only — do not list as Fall admit. Spring 2027 apps closed; Spring 2028 cycle opens later in 2026 per admissions hub.

items.program: Master of Science in Computational Finance (MSCF)

gre.detail: Official valid GRE or GMAT required (not both). Scores within 5 years and valid at application; accept arrival within 2 weeks of deadline. Self-report highest; GRE program code 7383. Application not reviewed without official score.

gmat.detail: GMAT accepted in lieu of GRE (code MSCF/Tepper 69H-XH-17). Either GRE or GMAT required.

toefl.detail: International candidates must take Duolingo, TOEFL (code B522 Carnegie Mellon–MSCF), or IELTS unless waiver criteria met. Scores valid 2 years at application. No numeric minimum posted on MSCF admissions page.

ielts.detail: Accepted; select Carnegie Mellon University and Computational Finance. Minimum not posted on MSCF admissions page.

english.waiver: Waiver if ≥2 years at undergrad institution earning bachelor’s where sole language of instruction was English (by Jul 31 of entry-year context per page wording—verify cycle year) OR graduate degree taught entirely in English. Documentation rules apply for non-U.S./non-English-official-language countries.

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA on MSCF admissions page; class profile shows average GPA 3.80 (descriptive, not a cutoff).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three LORs; prefer ability to speak to math/stats/CS/applied finance, English communication, teamwork. Recent students: ≥1 academic; prefer ≥1 professional. App not forwarded until all 3 received.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Two short-answer essays (350 words max each) after selecting post-MSCF career path; plus required 90-second video essay; optional essay ≤2 pages.

resume.detail: 1–2 pages; standard 12-pt font; must include month/year start and end for each position.

transcripts.detail: Upload legible scans of official transcripts/degree certificates for ALL institutions (incl. exchange/transfer). Internet printouts/unofficial copies not accepted for upload standard stated. Non-English: official translation; WES evaluations not accepted (WES standards as guideline only). Official sealed upon admit.

interview.detail: Invite-only on-campus or Zoom; requests for interview not considered. Clarifies quant prep, career fit, professional communication.

applicationFee.waivers: Fee waived for reapplicants who applied for 2026 when reapplying for Fall 2027.
applicationFee.detail: $125 payable online by credit card at submission.

other: Prerequisites: Calc I–II, linear algebra, calculus-based probability, ≥1 semester OOP (C++/Java/Python/C#); remediation before enrollment possible.
Four-year bachelor’s or foreign equivalent required before start.
Fall-only; mandatory on-campus Orientation from Aug 1.
Fall 2027 rounds: R1 Dec 1 2026; R2 Mar 1 2027.
applicationRequirements.advice: Fall-only with Aug 1 orientation and required summer internship path. GRE/GMAT hard required.

items.program: Master of Science in Financial Engineering (MFE)

gre.detail: GRE/GMAT no longer required; no place on application to submit scores; if attached separately they will not be taken into account. All applicants take Quantitative Background Assessment (QBA) instead.

gmat.detail: Same as GRE: not accepted / not considered; QBA replaces standardized tests.

toefl.detail: TOEFL scores are not required. English communication assessed at admission interviews.

ielts.detail: Not required per MFE application-process page.

english.waiver: N/A — English tests not required; assessed in interviews.

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA stated; baccalaureate from accredited 4-year U.S. college or foreign equivalent required.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three letters from individuals who can comment on skills for MFE success; no requirement that one be professor or industry.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Personal essay must answer: why Financial Engineering; why Baruch MFE; envisioned career path after graduating.

resume.detail: Not explicitly listed on current Fall 2027 application-process page (older Weissman PDF mentioned resume). Confirm live application checklist.

transcripts.detail: Scan transcripts from ALL schools attended into one file and upload. Official transcripts required only after admission offer.

interview.detail: Two virtual Zoom interview rounds before offer; primarily technical (math, finance, C++). Selected applicants contacted; cannot request interview.

applicationFee.detail: Current Fall 2027 MFE application-process page does not state fee amount. Older Weissman graduate application instructions PDF listed $75 non-refundable (also contained outdated GRE language)—treat fee as unconfirmed until live portal/Weissman confirms.

other: Mandatory Quantitative Background Assessment (QBA): Calculus, Linear Algebra, Probability, Finance, Brainteasers; online timed; open book; no internet/AI; honor code.
Prerequisites (B or better): Calc 2 semesters; Probability 1; Linear Algebra 1; C++ 1 semester/certificate; Finance 1 semester or relevant work.
Fall-only admission; Fall 2027 rounds Nov 1 / Dec 1 / Jan 15 / Mar 15 (plus Apr 1 for Spring Pre-MFE seminar students only).
Apply in only one round per year.
applicationRequirements.advice: GRE/GMAT not accepted—prepare for QBA + technical interviews. English tests not required.

gre.detail: Columbia Engineering: GRE not required for 2027 admission cycle (Spring 2027 and Fall 2027). Scores may be submitted optionally; non-submitters not penalized. Official scores required if admitted and scores were provided. School code 2111. IEOR FAQ still advises preparing GRE historically—policy for 2027 is optional.

gmat.detail: IEOR FAQ: GMAT not a requirement; may be included as supplementary material with personal statement file.

toefl.detail: Required if undergrad degree earned outside Australia, Canada, Ghana, Ireland, Kenya, New Zealand, Nigeria, Singapore, UK, USA (incl. transfers/joint programs). TOEFL iBT/Home, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, or Duolingo accepted (one test). No hard minimum to apply; IEOR notes may need to improve English if TOEFL ≤4.5 (post-Jan 21 2026 scale) or ≤99 (pre), IELTS ≤7.5, PTE ≤68, DET ≤130.

ielts.detail: Accepted as one of the English options under Engineering rules above.

english.waiver: Exception if master’s earned/will be completed in Australia, Canada, Ghana, Ireland, Kenya, New Zealand, Nigeria, Singapore, UK, or USA. Application also guides based on background. IEOR: waive if entirety of undergrad or graduate degree in an English-speaking country (per FAQ).

gpa.detail: IEOR FAQ: 3.0/4.0 GPA preferred; most successful applicants above 3.0. Not a hard stated cutoff.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three LORs. ≥2 academic unless bachelor’s earned >5 years before application (then academic strongly encouraged but not required).

transcripts.detail: Transcripts from every post-secondary institution attended; translations if not issued in English.

interview.detail: Mandatory Video Interview for MS applications after submit + fee paid (Status Portal): 3 random behavioral questions; 90 seconds to consider; 3 minutes to record answers to all three. Engineering overview also notes an additional interview may be requested.

applicationFee.waivers: Possible for U.S. citizens/PR enrolled in U.S. school with financial need and U.S. military/veterans via Application Fee Waiver Request Form.

other: ≠ columbia-msfe (CBS). This id is IEOR Engineering MSFE.
MSFE Fall start only (IEOR FAQ).
MSFE prep: calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics; differential equations helpful; Python essential; finance concepts (derivatives, risk, portfolio, markets).
Publications optional.
Only one Columbia Engineering program application per term.
applicationRequirements.advice: Distinguish from CBS columbia-msfe. Video interview is mandatory for MS. GRE optional for Fall 2027 Engineering cycle.
sources: IEOR Master of Science Admissions FAQs

items.program: MS in Quantitative and Computational Finance (MS-QCF)

gre.detail: Official GRE or GMAT required unless waived: 4-year U.S. undergrad GPA ≥3.7 OR Ph.D. Scores valid 5 years; higher quant score used if multiple. Institute GRE/TOEFL code 5248. Unofficial OK to evaluate; official needed before offer.

gmat.detail: GMAT accepted (code HWK-54-37) but applicants with GMAT must apply through College of Business home unit. Same waiver rules as GRE.

toefl.detail: TOEFL or IELTS only (Duolingo not accepted per QCF FAQ). GT Catalog: TOEFL iBT overall ≥4.5 (Speaking ≥3.5; Writing/Listening/Reading ≥4) on new scale; page notes prior iBT 90 ≈ 4.5. Also degree-from-approved-country or English-medium institution pathways.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (Writing 5.5; Speaking/Listening/Reading 6.5) per GT Catalog.

english.waiver: GT Catalog approved methods: degree from approved-country institution; degree from English-medium institution (MOI letter may be required); USG campus ESL completion; or meeting TOEFL/IELTS minima. QCF international page highlights collegiate degree where English was sole official language of instruction.

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA; holistic review with emphasis on quantitative coursework and quant test scores (QCF FAQ).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three recommenders (academic and/or professional). Minimum 2 of 3 needed for Grad Education to forward application.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Essay ≤750 words on academic/professional motivation and post-degree career vision; plus short-answers (project ≤750; programming ≤500; optional weaknesses ≤250).

transcripts.detail: Unofficial transcripts uploaded; official may be required if admitted. International: native + English translations of transcripts and degree docs.

interview.detail: Competitive candidates invited to ~30-minute behavioral Zoom interview with Associate Director (resume/projects/academic history).

applicationFee.waivers: QCF states it does not provide application fee waivers.

other: U.S.-equivalent 4-year bachelor’s required.
Quant background: Calc I–III, linear algebra, probability & statistics, differential equations; programming preferred (Python/R/C++/SAS).
Fall and Spring enrollment; Fall traditional ~1.5 yr with summer internship.
Fall 2027 deadlines: Early Oct 15 2026; Standard Dec 5 2026; Final intl outside US Mar 15 2027; Final US/PR/intl-in-US May 1 2027 (closes May 15).
applicationRequirements.advice: GRE/GMAT required except U.S. 3.7+/PhD waiver. Duolingo not accepted.

gre.detail: GRE not required; welcome to enhance application. Self-report then official ETS (institution 1832; dept 0799 Mathematical Science–Other). Valid if exam within 5 years of deadline.

gmat.detail: Do not submit GMAT scores (or high school transcripts, theses, publications)—not considered.

toefl.detail: TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic required unless exception. PSD policy minimum TOEFL 90 or IELTS 7; FinMath prefers significantly higher. Exams within 2 years of deadline. TOEFL code 1832 / dept 72.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic (not General Training) accepted; minimum 7 per PSD policy.

english.waiver: Waived if (a) English primary language of communication/schooling since childhood; OR (b) ≥1 academic year full-time at accredited English-medium post-secondary in listed countries/territories within past 10 years (incl. Antigua, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Hong Kong, Ireland, Jamaica, NZ, St. Kitts/Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent, Singapore, South Africa, Trinidad & Tobago, UK, USA). English-medium elsewhere / high school / part-time-research-only do not qualify.

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA stated on application-requirements page.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three letters; at least one professional reference.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Three candidate statements ≤250 words each (shortcoming/steps; program-city-career alignment; additional profile info).

resume.detail: Resume/CV with entire work history including start/end dates, locations, full- vs part-time.

transcripts.detail: Transcripts from all previous colleges/universities. Unofficial uploads for review; official final with degree conferral before enrollment if admitted.

interview.detail: No live interview listed among required documents. Two video statements are required application components (not a live interview).

other: Two video statements required.
Math prereqs: multivariable calculus, linear algebra, probability; programming ideally C++/Python/OOP.
Work experience encouraged but not required.
In-person Autumn 2027 rounds: Nov 2 2026; Feb 1 2027. Online also January/June starts.
applicationRequirements.advice: In-person is Autumn start; online has Jan/June starts. GMAT not accepted. GRE optional.

gre.detail: Official general GRE required for M.S. (FT and PT). Subject GRE in math/physics/other quant encouraged. Highly quantitative PhD holders may email cims-mathfin-app@nyu.edu with transcript to request GRE waiver. GSAS code 2596. Most accepted students >90th percentile quant (descriptive).

gmat.detail: GMAT not accepted for standard M.S. (Courant admissions page). Dual MathFin/MBA may use GMAT or GRE for GSAS; GMAT otherwise not a substitute for GRE per GSAS test-scores page.

toefl.detail: TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo required unless native English, U.S. citizen/PR, or baccalaureate/master’s at English-instruction institution. GSAS recommends TOEFL ≥100 (legacy) / ≥5 (new scale from Jan 2026), DET ≥130, IELTS ≥7; lower scores may still apply. Code 2596; TOEFL Essentials/ITP not accepted.

ielts.detail: IELTS accepted; GSAS recommends overall band ≥7.

english.waiver: Native English speaker; OR U.S. citizen/PR; OR completed/will complete baccalaureate or master’s where language of instruction is English (supporting letter if transcript unclear).

gpa.detail: No required minimum GPA (Courant admissions FAQ).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three LORs; ≥2 from instructors of advanced math/quant/CS/engineering. FT: ≥1 math-focused and ≥1 CS/programming-focused preferred. Manager letter OK if significant work experience.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Three topics ≤150 words each (career motivation; interesting math/science fact; research/class/internship). Optional separate Personal Statement for extra info.
statementOfPurpose.alsoKnownAs: statement of purpose / statement of academic purpose

resume.detail: Professional CV/resume with education, employment (company/division/dates/location/responsibilities), non-academic activities.

transcripts.detail: One official academic transcript from each post-secondary institution (upload in online application); official scores/transcripts needed to complete review.

interview.detail: Full-time applicants must submit a short video statement (≤5 minutes) addressing a challenging experience/project relevance to quant finance OR a preferred quant-finance area and fit. Not a live interview; required application video.

applicationFee.waivers: Not stated on Courant admissions page.

other: FT Fall-only (deadline Feb 12); PT Aug 1 Fall / Dec 1 Spring.
After submit: no updated grades/resumes/experience accepted.
Apply to only one Courant Math Finance program at a time.
applicationRequirements.advice: GRE required (GMAT not accepted for standard MS). Required video statement for FT/PT MS.

items.program: MS Mathematical and Computational Finance (MCF track)

gre.detail: GRE not required; GRE scores will not be accepted or considered for MS or PhD application packets (ICME application + FAQ).

gmat.detail: GMAT not mentioned as an accepted substitute; ICME explicitly rejects GRE consideration. Treat GMAT as not part of ICME packet.

toefl.detail: Per Stanford Graduate Admissions: TOEFL iBT ≥90 (tests before Jan 21 2026) or ≥4.5 (on/after Jan 21 2026) unless exempt. ICME defers to central Grad Admissions.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic minimum 7 for admission consideration unless exempt.

english.waiver: Exempt if U.S. citizen/PR; first language English; U.S. bachelor’s/master’s/doctoral or international equivalent from university where all instruction in English; OR ≥2 consecutive years full-time professional/educational experience in English in past 10 years.

gpa.detail: Enter GPA as on transcript; do not convert scales. No ICME minimum stated.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Three required (optional 4th backup). Strongly recommend ≥1 from university professor; Interfolio not accepted; letters may arrive up to 1 week after deadline.

statementOfPurpose.detail: MS track: short-answer career goals / how CME-MS helps (program supplemental). Also Enriching the Learning Community ≤500 words. PhD-oriented SOP prompt on page is for PhD; MS uses supplemental short answers + academic interest MCF track selection.
statementOfPurpose.alsoKnownAs: statement / short answers / enriching the learning community

resume.detail: ICME requires CV/resume upload for complete application.

transcripts.detail: Unofficial transcript uploads for institutions attended ≥1 year full-time; official upon accept.

interview.detail: No interview listed among ICME MS application components on official application/FAQ pages.

applicationFee.waivers: GRE Fee Reduction, Program Participation, and School-Based waivers via Stanford Grad Admissions (request ≥10 business days before deadline). School of Engineering graduate fee waiver also referenced from ICME page.

other: Apply to ICME MS and select MCF track in program supplemental Academic Interest.
Required course-preparation form (list advanced math/CS/stats/etc.).
External MS Autumn 2027-28 deadline Jan 29 2027 11:59pm PST; admission Autumn only for external applicants.
HCP part-time option available for MS via SCPD.
applicationRequirements.advice: GRE not accepted. Select MCF track inside ICME MS application. Autumn-only for external applicants.
